title: Damson Jam
subtitle: Deep, tannic, intensely flavoured wild damson preserve
excerpt: Damsons are small, sour, and richly flavoured, a far more characterful jam than plum. The fruit is full of pectin, sets firmly, and needs only sugar and water. Makes about four 450 g jars.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton (PG #10136); Pam Corbin, Preserves. Damsons are high in pectin and tannin; the traditional sieve method removes the stones after cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze whole raw damsons — they're notoriously brief in season.

content.text: Damson jam is the one that makes other jams taste ordinary. The fruit is small and sour with an almost wine-dark skin, and the finished preserve has a depth and slight bitterness that nothing shop-bought replicates. Damsons are too small to stone cleanly before cooking, so they go in whole and the stones come out after. Makes about four 450 g jars.

Put the whole damsons and water in the jam pan over medium heat. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until the skins split and the fruit is completely soft, about 15 minutes. The stones will have separated from the pulp.
Add the sugar to the pan. As it begins to dissolve, scoop out stones as they float to the surface with a slotted spoon. It takes a few minutes to find them all. This is fiddly but necessary.

Once the sugar has dissolved and the stones are out, raise to a full rolling boil. Cook for 10 to 12 minutes. Test on a cold plate from 10 minutes,  damson jam sets readily due to the fruit's high pectin and tannin. Skim, rest 5 minutes, jar into hot sterilised jars and seal. Check the first few jars for any missed stones before putting away.

items.cause: Damsons contain more stones than plums relative to fruit volume.
items.fix: Stir the jam and watch carefully as you ladle. For future batches, the slotted-spoon stage is patient work, give it a full 5 minutes.

items.cause: Damsons are exceptionally high in pectin.
items.fix: Reduce sugar to 800 g per kg fruit, or check the set from 8 minutes. Even firm damson jam has a wonderful flavour.

items.cause: Some skins from underripe or late-picked fruit.
items.fix: Pick damsons when fully ripe in September. Cooking longer doesn't reduce the bitterness.

items.cause: Very unusual with damsons, but possible if fruit was water-logged after heavy rain.
items.fix: Return to the pan, add the juice of 1 lemon, boil another 5 minutes and test.
